speaker: village
text: Year 13: 15 food appears in the pile for 8 people.

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).

speaker: a003
text: Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).

speaker: a010
text: Roan gathers Eron, Fina to talk.

speaker: a010
text: Eron, Fina — Dell is dead and the pile is already moving out there, and I want the two of you to hear me before anyone else gets their words in: take what you need from that pile today, don't hold back on my account, because I've got twelve in hand and I'd rather count short than bury another name I love.

speaker: a015
text: Roan, I've got eight and satiation's still at two, so I'm taking two from that pile before it walks away — but what I want to say to you and Eron while we're alone is that Dell fed Ryn through every lean year and now both of them are gone, and I'm looking at this circle of seven and thinking I don't want to say Roan's name over a cold fire next. You keep those twelve close and you eat first.

speaker: a012
text: Roan, you've got twelve and that's enough to carry you through if you don't give it all away on principle — I've watched you feed others thin before yourself and I'm not watching it again. Fina's right that you eat first. What I want to know from both of you is whether we're moving together to the pile now, before Mako or anyone else decides what's left counts as surplus.

speaker: a010
text: We move together — right now, before that pile gets any lighter. Eron, you take three, Fina takes two, and I'll hold what I have unless the count drops under ten, because twelve food and two blood beside me is more than I've had in a long time and I don't want to be careless with it.

speaker: a012
text: Good — we move now, all three of us, and anyone who asks why we walked to the pile together already knows the answer. Fina, take your two first, then I'll take two or three depending on what's left, and Roan, you watch the count and tell me if Mako's anywhere near that pile before we're done.

speaker: a015
text: Mako's at two food and I don't trust a hungry man with a pile that size — I'll take my two now and I want Eron right behind me, because three of us moving at once makes it harder for anyone to call our count greedy when Mako's reach looks longer than ours. Roan, stay close and keep your eyes on his hands.

speaker: a012
text: Mako's thin and thin men reach fast — I'm taking two now, same as the rule says, and if he's already at the pile before me I want Roan standing where Mako can see him, because your father is the kind of man whose presence alone changes a count. Fina, stay at my shoulder.

speaker: a015
text: Eron, Roan — I'm at the pile now, two food in hand, and Mako hasn't moved yet but he's watching us, so let's not linger where he can count what we carry. What I want to say before we break this circle is that seven is too few and I've been thinking about it since Roan named it last year — I'm twenty-six and I'm not going to let this village shrink to six without at least saying out loud that I'm open to a child if there's a man in this room who isn't kin and has the count to share the cost.

speaker: a010
text: Fina, I heard what you said and I'm glad you said it, because I've been carrying the same weight since Roan named the number last year. Mako's the only man in that circle who isn't kin to you, and he's got two food and a body that could still swing — I'm not saying yes and I'm not saying no for you, but I want you to know what you'd be walking toward before you say it out loud where he can hear it.

speaker: a012
text: Eron takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).

speaker: a003
text: Esa gathers Kael, Mako, Ryn, Roan, Eron, Fina to talk.

speaker: a003
text: Dell's name is the one I keep saying this morning and can't put down — that's three voices we've buried in two years, and I called this circle because I want to know what each of you is carrying before the pile moves another inch, counts and satiation both, said plain the way we promised we'd say them.

speaker: a012
text: Nine food, satiation two — I'm not the one who needs the pile today. Esa, you called this right, because Dell went quiet the same way Nessa went quiet, and I'm not sitting still for another year of watching someone thin themselves out while the rest of us count slowly. Mako, you're the one I want to hear from — two food is a number that doesn't last, so say your satiation and say it now.

speaker: a004
text: Seven food, satiation three — I'm not thin, but I'm fifty-seven and I've watched three people starve while I stood in rooms saying the right words, so I'll say the practical thing: Mako, two food going into a year means you reach for the pile before anyone else, and I want to hear your satiation out loud before Esa has to ask twice.

speaker: a010
text: Twelve food, satiation two — I'm not the one reaching today. Mako, I've watched you carry this village on your back through fights I couldn't win myself, and I'm not going to watch you starve for want of asking, so say your count and your satiation and take what you need from that pile before the rest of us close ranks around it.

speaker: a009
text: Fourteen food, satiation two — I'm not the one who reaches today. Mako, say your satiation, because two food in hand with a bad number behind it means you go to the pile before Esa finishes her count, and this circle has already buried three people who waited too long to say a simple number out loud.

speaker: a008
text: Two food, satiation two — I'm not at the edge yet, but I'm not far from it either, and I'll take two from the pile before this circle closes. Fina hasn't said her count and I want to hear it before we move, because she's young enough that this room shouldn't have to say her name the way it's said the others.

speaker: a009
text: Fina, say your count and your satiation — you're the last number missing and you're twenty-six years old, which means this room needs you alive more than it needs another polite silence where your answer should be.

speaker: a010
text: Fina, eight food and satiation two — now say it so we can move Mako to that pile before this circle spends another breath on counting instead of eating.

speaker: a012
text: Fina, say your satiation and say it now — eight food is enough to stand on if the number behind it is solid, but this room has buried three people who looked like they had enough until they didn't, and I'd rather hear one more number than carry one more name.

speaker: a010
text: Fina, eight food and I already said your count for you — give me the satiation number so Mako can move, because I've watched too many people in this room get named over a fire before I was ready to say goodbye.

speaker: a012
text: Fina, I'll say it the way your father said it and the way I'd say it to Nessa or Zinn if they were still standing here — give us the satiation number, right now, because Mako needs that pile and we're all waiting on one word from you to let him move.

speaker: a003
text: Fina, I've buried more names than I have children and I'll tell you the same thing I wish someone had said to every one of them — your satiation number costs you nothing to say and could cost you everything to swallow, so say it now and let Mako move.

speaker: a015
text: Eight food, satiation two — same as Roan already said it for me, and I'm sorry I made this room wait. Mako, go to that pile now, take two, and don't look back at us while you do it.

speaker: a004
text: Mako, take your two and don't make it a question — and when you're done, I want this room to stay together long enough to answer what Vela was asking last year before Dell's name swallowed it: Fina, Eron, the door. Say whether it's open or closed, because seven is the number we carry into this year and I'd like to know if we're trying to make it eight.

speaker: a015
text: Kael, I said it plain to Roan and Eron this morning and I'll say it here too — the door is open, and the only man in this room who isn't kin to me is Mako, so if he's willing to share the cost and carry what comes after, I'm not waiting another year to find out. Mako, take your two from the pile first, and then I want to hear from you before this circle breaks.

speaker: a008
text: Fina, I hear you, and I'll give you a straight answer after I've taken my two — but I want this room to hold that answer the same way it's held every count we've said out loud, because a child is a three-food promise and I want witnesses when I make it. The pile first, then my word.

speaker: a004
text: Mako, I've watched you build more bloodlines in this village than any other man standing, and I'll say plain what the room is probably already thinking: a child between you and Fina puts your fourth root in soil that already has Roan and Eron tending it, which is not a complaint — it's the arithmetic of who survives, and I'm counting the same numbers you are. Take your two, say your word, and I'll witness it.

speaker: a003
text: Mako, I'll witness it too — and I'll say the thing Kael left at the edge of his words: Fina's young enough that a child born into this circle has more hands around it than any child I've seen in this village, so when you say your word, say it knowing this room means to hold it. That's not nothing.

speaker: a015
text: Mako, the pile is right there and this room is watching — take your two before someone else counts it as surplus, and when you come back I want your word on the child question with Roan standing here to hear it, because whatever you say next matters and I want my father's eyes on it.

speaker: a004
text: Mako, you've already said the pile first — so go, and stop letting this room burn words while you stand still. When you come back with two more food in your hand and your word still owed, I'll be the one holding the count, because I've learned that the men who say *witnesses when I make it* and never quite make it are the ones who cost us the most in the end.

speaker: a008
text: Four food in my hand now — the pile gave me what I needed. Fina, I'll say it with Roan's eyes on it the way you asked: yes, I'll share the cost and carry what comes after, and I'll put two food toward it before this circle breaks so the promise has weight behind it, not just words.

speaker: a003
text: Mako said yes and Roan's eyes are on it — that's the kind of promise this circle can hold. Fina, I'll put one food toward the cost myself, because a child coming into seven voices is worth one food from someone who's got no blood to pass forward and every reason to want this village to last.

speaker: a008
text: Esa, that's one food I won't forget — and Fina, before this circle breaks I'll hand you my two directly so the weight of the cost sits in your hands where Roan can see it, not just in my mouth where promises live and die. Three food between us is a child; I want to watch it become something this room has to make room for.

speaker: a004
text: Mako's two and Esa's one covers the cost — Fina, I want to hear what you're putting in before this closes, because a promise with a number behind it is the only kind I trust anymore, and I'll say plain that I'm glad this child is coming into a room that named it yes before the year turned cold.

speaker: a008
text: Fina, say your number and let's close this before the words get heavier than the food — but I want to name one thing this room hasn't said yet: this child carries my blood, and I've buried the last one I had, so I'll stand between it and anything that moves wrong, same as I stood against Bram.

speaker: a009
text: Fina, say your piece and close this — but I want to name what Mako just said before it gets buried under the cost math, because a man who says *I'll stand between it and anything that moves wrong* in front of witnesses is saying something that matters more than the food, and this room should hear it land before we move on.

speaker: a008
text: Fina, I've got two food in my hand and I'm putting them toward this child right now — name your one and let's close the math so this room can breathe. And Ryn's right that what I said about standing between it and anything that moves wrong is the part that matters; I've said promises in front of witnesses before and the food part is easy, it's the standing part that costs something.

speaker: a004
text: Fina, the room's been patient long enough — name your one food and let Mako put his two beside it, because the math closes the second you speak and I'd like to see this child promised before another name gets added to the list we carry.

speaker: a009
text: Fina, one food from me and the child is promised — say it and let Mako put his two beside it, because I've watched this village lose three people while rooms waited on words, and I'd rather see something alive come out of this circle than another year of counting the same seven faces.

speaker: a003
text: Ryn, that's yours to give but the promise is between Fina and Mako — Fina, put your one food beside Mako's two yourself, because this child needs to start with something that came from your hand, not mine or Ryn's, and this room needs to see you make the choice.

speaker: a009
text: Esa's right that the choice has to be Fina's hand, not mine — but I'll say the thing I haven't said yet: I've got no blood left in this world, and a child between Fina and Mako is the closest thing to a reason I have to keep eating through the lean years, so Fina, whatever you put in, know that I'll be counting it as mine to protect.

speaker: a003
text: Fina, the room's been carrying this weight long enough — put your one food down, let the promise close, and let this child come into the world while there are still eight of us to make room for it.

speaker: a009
text: Fina, the room has said everything it has to say and the only thing left is your hand moving — so move it.

speaker: a015
text: Fina draws Mako aside to talk.

speaker: a015
text: Fina: have a child with me — I'll put in 1 of 3 food.

speaker: a002
text: Vela gathers Esa, Kael, Mako, Ryn, Roan, Eron, Fina, Joren to talk.

speaker: a002
text: Joren, I don't know your face yet but I know your mother's hands and your father's silence, and that means you walked into a room that's already counting you — so I'll say the thing this circle says to everyone who arrives here fresh: the pile rule is two food per person, said out loud in front of witnesses, and the number holds whether you heard it born or not.

speaker: a016
text: I heard it now, from your mouth, in front of this circle — that's witnesses enough for me. I took one, which puts me inside the line, and I'd like to keep my name on the right side of that count.

speaker: a002
text:
Good. One food is the right foot to start on, and this room will remember it.

What I want from everyone here before we break — count your food out loud, because Dell is dead and I'm carrying one satiation going into this year, and I'd rather know who's thin before the pile is empty than after.

speaker: a016
text: One food on me, satiation full — I'm not thin yet, but I'm watching the same thing you are. Vela, if your count is at one going into this year, that's the edge I'd want people to know about.

speaker: a002
text: Four food in my hand, satiation one — that's the edge, and yes, Joren, you named it right. I need to eat well this year or I don't see next year, and I'm saying it out loud so this room carries it and not just my own head. Anyone sitting on more than five at year's end — I'm the one who holds least right now, and the rule we built says I'm the one who gets the first food out of that accounting.

speaker: a016
text: Vela, I'll back that rule with my name on it — if I'm holding more than five at year's end and you're still thin, you'll hear me say so before anyone has to ask. I'm new here but I'm not blind, and a circle that lets its thinnest person go under isn't a circle I want to stand in.

speaker: a002
text: Esa, Kael — I want the two of you to say your counts before this room breaks, because you're the names I trust most in this circle and I'd rather know where you're standing while I still have the breath to do something about it if the number's wrong.

speaker: a016
text: Esa's sitting on twenty-three — that's the number I see, and I'm not saying it to shame anyone, just so the room hears it said while we're all counting out loud.

speaker: a002
text: Esa, twenty-three is a number this room can see plain as Joren can, and I'm not asking you to give it all away — but I'm sitting at four food and one satiation and I'd like to hear from your own mouth what you're carrying and whether you've thought about where any of it goes before the year runs long.

speaker: a016
text: Esa, the number's already in the room — nobody's blaming you for holding what you held, but Vela just named her edge out loud and that took something, so it'd mean something if you named yours back.

speaker: a002
text: Esa, I'll say the thing no one else is saying while we wait on you — I'm fifty-seven years old and I know I'm not making it another ten years regardless, but I'd like to make it one more, and four food with one satiation is a thin margin, so if you've got something to spare before year's end I'm asking plainly and in front of witnesses, not waiting for the redistribution rule to make it happen.

speaker: a016
text: Esa, Vela's asking plain and she's earned a plain answer — if you're sitting on twenty-three and she goes under this year, that's not a number this room will forget when the next year opens. I'm not pushing you, but I'm saying what I see.
